clue.text: New batter collects one special cap

indicators.note: to collect is to gather in, so the reworked batter takes the next item inside itself
something new has been remade, so the letters of batter come out in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cricketer new to the side is handed a special cap for the occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: A biretta is the square, three-ridged cap worn by Roman Catholic clergy, a headgear reserved for a special role.

clue.text: Wild animals getting bugs

definitions.meaning: first meaning: burrowing black-and-white striped mammals
second meaning: pesters or nags, a verb

explanation.surface: Animals in the wild picking up insects or infections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bugs' reads as insects or germs, but it is the verb meaning to annoy persistently.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural noun names the striped mammals, and the same spelling is the verb form meaning harasses or pesters someone.

clue.text: Upright type, member of an empire

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the ordinary non-italic typeface
second meaning: a citizen of the ancient empire ruled from Rome

explanation.surface: An honest, upstanding sort of person belonging to some empire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upright type' suggests an honest person, but here it is printing: the plain vertical typeface as opposed to italic.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman is the printers' name for standard upright lettering, and also a citizen of ancient Rome's empire.

clue.text: Start to pick up and go round?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: begin to recover after a bad period
second meaning: literally steer around a bend or street corner

explanation.surface: Instructions perhaps for a driver: get moving and take the bend.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to pass the worst point and begin improving, while its literal sense is driving round a bend in the road.

clue.text: Drink containing very soft fruit

indicators.note: something containing another holds it inside, so the drink wraps around the next item

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
pianissimo, the musical marking for very soft

explanation.surface: A beverage with mushy fruit floating in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very soft' looks like a description of the fruit, but it is the musical marking.
explanation.definitionFit: An apple is a common orchard fruit, a straightforward example of the category.

clue.text: Food for number to tuck into, as intended

indicators.note: to tuck into food is to go inside it, so the number goes within the food

parts.note: meat as a general word for food
N is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: A meal for several people to eat, just as planned.
explanation.definitionFit: Meant is the past participle of mean, so something meant was purposed or intended.

clue.text: Silly ladies' man, sort displaying ineptitude

indicators.note: something silly is muddled and nonsensical, so the following letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: A foolish womaniser type showing how clumsy he is.
explanation.definitionFit: Maladroitness is clumsiness or lack of skill, a close synonym of inept behaviour.

clue.text: Trade event with lots getting sold

definitions.text: Trade event with lots getting sold

parts.words: Trade event with lots getting sold
parts.note: surface reading: a busy fair where plenty of goods change hands
setter's reading: lots are the numbered items offered one by one to bidders

explanation.surface: A busy market where a great deal is sold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lots' seems to mean a large quantity, but it is the saleroom word for each item under the hammer.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a public sale where numbered items are offered to bidders and go to the highest offer.

clue.text: Like music in restaurant, on always

indicators.note: in says the wanted letters sit inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: spans the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Background music playing nonstop in a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonal describes sound organised around pitch or a key, as music is.

clue.text: Object, being not quite totally bashful?

indicators.note: not quite means falling just short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: demure means modest and shy

explanation.surface: A thing described as almost entirely shy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a noun, but it is the verb meaning to protest.
explanation.definitionFit: To demur is to raise an objection or show reluctance, a formal synonym of the verb object.

clue.text: Bird nice pal gets to fly

indicators.note: letters sent flying scatter and land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird whose friendly companion gets the chance to fly.
explanation.definitionFit: The pelican is a large water bird with a pouched bill, one example of a bird.

clue.text: An age in school? Time to escape!

indicators.note: whatever escapes gets out and is gone, so that letter leaves the word

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A pupil feels they have been at school forever and it is time to break out.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is an English boarding school near Windsor; take its T away.
explanation.definitionFit: An eon is an immeasurably long period, an age.

clue.text: Student finally gets to study philosopher — a dreary routine!

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: the closing letter of student
to read a subject is to study it at university
John Stuart Mill, the Victorian philosopher

explanation.surface: A student at last tackles philosophy, and finds it tedious.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadmill is figuratively any monotonous, wearying routine, from the exercise machine that goes nowhere.

clue.text: Meal is excellent with one portion doubled up

indicators.note: doubled up means one part is repeated, the copy set inside next to the original

parts.note: super means very good
one portion of the word, its middle letter, is copied

explanation.surface: A great dinner where one helping is twice the size.
explanation.definitionFit: Supper is an evening meal, a plain example of a meal.

clue.text: Long-suffering man or woman that is not heartless

indicators.note: with its heart removed a word loses its middle letter

parts.note: Pat is a name used by both men and women
i.e., Latin id est, meaning that is
taken as written, then gutted

explanation.surface: A tolerant person, neither man nor woman, who is never unkind.
explanation.definitionFit: Patient as an adjective means bearing delay or trouble calmly, which long-suffering also means.

clue.text: Instrument that plays my number the wrong way

parts.note: Cor! is a British exclamation of surprise, like My!

indicators.note: going the wrong way means running backwards, so the number is read in reverse

parts.note: ten is a number

explanation.surface: A musical instrument that butchers my favourite song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is not a possessive here but an exclamation, matching the British cry Cor!
explanation.definitionFit: The cornet is a brass instrument like a small trumpet, so an instrument that is played.

clue.text: Beastly female gets sir excited

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up and fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cruel woman manages to rouse a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beastly' suggests nasty, but it means belonging to the animal kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: A tigress is the female of the tiger, literally a female beast.

clue.text: A swagger, when rounding on a long-distance traveller

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: rounding something means going all the way around it, so the swagger wraps the next words

parts.note: a strut is a proud, swaggering walk
taken as written

explanation.surface: A boastful walk shown by someone setting out on a long journey.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronaut travels into space, the longest distance any traveller covers.

clue.text: Fools to judge, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means all but a bit, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: to assess is to evaluate or judge

explanation.surface: Idiots, mostly, should do the judging.
explanation.definitionFit: Asses is a common informal word for stupid people, from the donkey's reputation.

clue.text: Units of land in mostly sacred ground

indicators.note: something ground is crushed and broken up, so the letters are rearranged
mostly means all but the end, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: taken as written, then shortened

explanation.surface: Measured plots of land inside a churchyard or other holy ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sacred ground' reads as a holy site, but 'ground' is the signal to mix the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a traditional measure of land area, roughly 4,047 square metres.

clue.text: Brute very holy? Minimally good

parts.note: pi is slang for pious, excessively religious

indicators.note: minimally means as little as possible, so just the first letter of the next word

parts.note: the opening letter of good

explanation.surface: A savage who seems devout, but only barely decent.
explanation.walkthrough: PI, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for holy.
explanation.definitionFit: Pig is a colloquial insult for a coarse, brutish person.

clue.text: Perch outside old coastal town

parts.note: a perch is an old unit of length, the same as a pole or rod

explanation.walkthrough: 'Perch' suggests the fish or a bird's roost, but it is the old measure of length.
explanation.definitionFit: Poole is a harbour town on the Dorset coast in southern England.

clue.text: Less friendly, showing back to monarch once

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship
Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen Elizabeth II

explanation.surface: A former king turning his back, being cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterner is the comparative of stern, harsher and more severe, so less warm or friendly.

clue.text: Escape to a match?

parts.note: surface reading: slipping away to watch a game
setter's reading: a match is a marriage, so this is running off secretly to wed

explanation.surface: Sneaking off to a football game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' points to sport, but here it means a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: To elope is to run away secretly with a lover in order to marry.

clue.text: Instrument seen with celebrity around India

parts.note: a star is a celebrity

clue.text: Resists nasty relations

indicators.note: something nasty is twisted or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone holding out against unpleasant family members.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisters are female siblings, a kind of family relation.
